rootCause.details: Both implementations identify the unconditional space passed to the terminal input function as the source of the empty-suffix rendering defect. The solver treats an empty suffix as a special case and passes an empty string, while the accepted fix preserves the readline safeguard by splitting the fully built prompt: echo all but its final character, then pass that final character to the input function. The solver therefore fixes the reported display but not the complete terminal-input invariant addressed by the accepted patch.

behavior.details:
Empty and default suffixes render identically in both implementations. A direct custom-suffix counterexample diverges: prompt_suffix='>' renders 'test> foo
' for prompt and 'test> y
' for confirm under the solver, but 'test>foo
' and 'test>y
' under the accepted fix. The accepted implementation treats prompt_suffix as the complete suffix and adds no extra character. For an empty suffix, the solver also calls the input function with '', whereas the accepted fix calls it with the last prompt character, retaining the readline backspace workaround without changing the composed display.

tests.details: The solver's six-case matrix encodes the divergent custom-suffix output as expected behavior, asserting an extra space after '>'. It verifies final CliRunner output but not which final prompt character is routed through the input function, so it cannot detect loss of the readline workaround in the empty case. The accepted regression uses file-descriptor capture around the terminal input emulation and covers prompt and confirm on stdout and stderr.

scope.details: The solver is localized to the same two input sites and adds symmetric tests, but its branch is narrower than the accepted behavioral correction and omits the accepted API documentation and changelog note that a space is no longer appended. Its custom-suffix expectation preserves the pre-fix unconditional space rather than the accepted prompt_suffix contract.

simplicity.details: Both implementations are small and readable. The accepted text[:-1]/text[-1:] formulation is branch-free and maintains a single invariant for empty, default, and custom suffixes; the solver's explicit empty-string condition is also easy to understand but is behaviorally incomplete.

regressions.details: The submitted and full practical suites pass, but direct comparison exposes two missed edges: non-space custom suffixes retain an unwanted appended space, and the empty-suffix path no longer supplies any character through the input function for the readline safeguard. These differences occur in both prompt and confirm.

limitations: The readline backspace effect requires an interactive readline terminal and was not reproduced end-to-end in this non-interactive audit; the call-argument divergence and accepted implementation establish that the solver bypasses the safeguard.
The decisive custom-suffix outputs were reproduced directly on Python 3.12/Linux; the complete supported interpreter and Windows matrices were not rerun.
Repair should route the final character of the fully built prompt through the input function for every suffix, update the custom-suffix expectations, and retain symmetric prompt/confirm coverage.
